faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives gross annual pay before tax and super. Remember that this assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?

On our timesheet, you can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add 25% casual loading on top – do not enter a rate that already includes the loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a registered nurse?

The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a registered nurse earning above that threshold, super only applies to the first $270,830 of ordinary earnings.

## Converting a Registered Nurse Salary QLD Per Hour

If you’re a registered nurse in Queensland looking to understand your pay, you’ve probably asked: what is the **registered nurse salary qld per hour**? While there is no single median figure for this role, we can use reliable benchmarks from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) and the Fair Work Ombudsman to help you convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the standard under the National Employment Standards), the formula becomes:

**Annual = hourly × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $50, your annual gross pay would be $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This is a simple estimate; it assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Queensland Full-Time Ordinary Time Earnings

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings report for May 2026 shows that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Queensland were $2,039.70 per week. Dividing by 38 hours gives an hourly equivalent of approximately $53.68. This is an **average** for all full-time workers in Queensland, not a median for registered nurses. Actual rates for nurses depend on your classification under the *Nurses Award 2020*, your experience, and whether you work shifts that attract penalties.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

To find your fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay. If you earn $50 per hour for 38 hours, your weekly pay is $1,900 and your fortnightly pay is $3,800. This can be useful for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time employee (38 hours per week). For casual workers, the minimum is $33.05 per hour including the 25% casual loading. Registered nurses are covered by the *Nurses Award 2020*, which sets minimum rates for different classifications (e.g., Registered Nurse Level 1, Level 2, etc.). These award rates are higher than the minimum wage. You can check the specific award rates on the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) for your classification. Remember that award rates are minimums; many nurses earn above them.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual registered nurse, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of your base hourly rate. On our [the timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and tick a checkbox to add the 25% casual loading automatically. Do **not** enter a rate that already includes the loading – the tool will calculate it correctly.

### Tax and Superannuation

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed). Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a registered nurse earning $98,800, super would add about $11,856 per year, but this is not deducted from your pay.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Queensland’s average full-time ordinary time earnings of $2,039.70 per week are slightly below the national average of $2,083.70 per week (ABS, May 2026). This difference reflects industry mix and cost-of-living factors. When comparing a registered nurse salary QLD per hour to other states, keep in mind that award rates are national, but actual market rates can vary. For more detailed comparisons, see our [reference tables](/data).

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your hourly rate and instantly see annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. You can also toggle casual loading and see an estimate of tax and super. It’s a quick way to check what a job offer means in real terms.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
